themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaint Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints exploded to 7 this week versus 0.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1,767% spike (z-score: 13.68)—suggesting either rapid expansion of streetside dining operations or mounting resident friction with existing venues in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights.
evidence: 7 outdoor dining complaints this week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,767% increase)
Z-score of 13.68 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
No recent local news coverage or Reddit discussion yet—story is breaking now
reporting_angles: Are new outdoor dining permits being issued or shantis expanded? Check DOE and CB5 records.
Interview residents near high-complaint areas (likely Williamsburg/Fort Greene waterfront): what is driving complaints—noise, waste, overcrowding, lack of permits?

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints reached 7 this week, up 522% from a baseline of 1.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting a potential sanitation or pest management crisis or seasonal die-off linked to weather/construction.
evidence: 7 dead animal complaints this week vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (522% increase)
Z-score of 6.34 indicates significant statistical deviation
1,233 recent building permits (882 alterations) may indicate disruption to animal habitats or sanitation
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine if this reflects a specific neighborhood cluster or citywide trend.
Investigate whether recent construction activity (high permit volume) is displacing rodents or other urban wildlife into residential areas.

themes_detail.label: Real-Time Enforcement Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Real-time enforcement complaints jumped to 11 this week, up 1,157% from a 0.9 weekly baseline over 8 weeks (z-score: 6.27)—indicating either new or aggressive enforcement operations (parking, vending, traffic) that are generating resident backlash.
evidence: 11 real-time enforcement complaints this week vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,157% increase)
Separate spike in IAD complaints (4 vs. 0.2 baseline, z-score 8.66) suggests possible enforcement misconduct or policy changes
reporting_angles: Has NYPD, DOT, or DOC issued new enforcement directives or deployed additional officers to CD302 this week?

Interview residents and business owners about specific enforcement encounters: Are officers conducting stops for parking, vending, quality-of-life infractions? Are they perceived as fair or aggressive?

themes_detail.label: Residential Disposal Complaint Jump
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints surged to 11 this week, up 283% from a 2.9 weekly baseline—suggesting either a change in trash collection service, accumulation due to holiday season, or new waste management issues in specific buildings.
evidence: 11 residential disposal complaints this week vs. 2.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (283% increase)
Concurrent dead animal spike may indicate broader sanitation infrastructure strain
reporting_angles: Check DSNY schedules: Have collection routes changed, been delayed, or reduced in CD302 this week?
Are complaints concentrated in a specific neighborhood or building type? Map 311 complaints to identify hotspots.

themes_detail.label: Construction Lead Dust Concerns
themes_detail.summary: Construction lead dust complaints hit 4 two weeks ago, up 540% from a 0.6 weekly baseline—combined with 1,233 recent DOB permits (882 alterations), this signals potential lead remediation gaps or inadequate dust control at renovation sites.
evidence: 4 construction lead dust complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (540% increase)
1,233 active DOB permits filed in last 90 days, heavily weighted toward alterations (882), creating potential lead exposure at scale
reporting_angles: Are DOB inspectors conducting pre-renovation lead assessments and monitoring dust containment on high-permit-volume blocks?
Interview residents and parents near active alteration sites: Are they experiencing respiratory issues, dust visible on windows/stoops, or notification of lead hazards?
